entry.dc:title: How a computer was used in evaluating the Vuonos nickel deposit in Finland
entry.dc:creator: PELTOLA E
entry.dc:description: Outokumpu Oy, Finland's largest mining company is developing an open pit adjacent to the old Outokumpu Mine, Vuonos deposit, containing only 0. 20% sulfide nickel. Vuonos will be the largest mine in the country, designed to produce annually 300,000 tonnes of Cu- , and 1,500,000 tonnes of Ni ores. Paper describes how a computer program was used to evaluate the marginal ore body and plan open pit mining.

entry.dc:title: Ptolemais, Greece's largest lignite mine trebles production
entry.dc:creator: KULLIK E
entry.dc:description: Open pit mining operation, located in northern Greece at the altitude of 2200 ft above sea level exploits a lignite seam of a thickness varying between 160 and 210 ft. Total reserves are estimated to amount to 350 million tonnes. Two grades of lignite are selectively mined- '%'A'%' suitable for briquetting with maximum 9% ash; and '%'B'%' with up to 13% ash, used for generation of electric power. In order to increase annual production of 2 million tonnes threefold, large bucket wheel excavators and steel cable reinforced, rubber belt conveying system of total length exceeding 10 mi. have been installed.

entry.dc:title: Geology and mining operations at Palabora Mining Company Limited, Phalaborwa, N- E Transvaal
entry.dc:creator: KUSCHKE OH
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of the South African Institute of Mining and Metallurgy
entry.dc:description: A description is given of the general geology, structure and minerals of economic significance of the Loolekop copper orebody at Phalaborwa. The open pit mining method is described with details of drilling, blasting loading, hauling and primary crushing operations. A brief description is given of mine planning and its relationship to the control of the mining operation.

entry.dc:title: Statistical methods of determining calculated loads of industrial plants, (Metody statystyczne wyznaczania obciazen obliczeniowych w zakladach przemyslowych)
entry.dc:creator: CZAJKOWSKI Z
entry.dc:description: Methods are discussed of determining calculated (peak) loads in industrial plants of open pit mining. Numerical values of calculation coefficients for various electric loads in brown coal strip mines are given.

entry.dc:title: Underground Coal mining, 1970
entry.dc:creator: ANON
entry.dc:description: Review of mining and minerals processing industries encompasses 21 articles covering- impact of Federal Coal Mine Health and Safety Acto of 1969 on underground coal mining; developments in coal preparation; underground mining; open pit mining; mineral exploration; bituminous coal economics; world metallurgical coal in 1970's; European coal report; the economic future of western fossil fuel; uranium requirements for light water reactors; phosphate- emergin trends; new markets for tomorrow's sulfur; copper- vital metal in an era of change; aluminum; outlook for world commerce in nonferrous metals; outlook for silver; strategic minerals of the future; ferroalloys- a billion dollar industry; and Japanese search for raw materials.

entry.dc:title: ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT FOR THE BELT CONVEYOR SYSTEMS USED IN THE PTOLEMAIS (GREECE) OPEN-CAST MINING OPERATIONS, (ELEKTRISCHE AUSRUESTUNG DER FOERDERBANDANLAGEN IM GRIECHISCHEN TAGEBAU PTOLEMAIS
entry.dc:creator: BOMMER R
entry.dc:description: At this open pit mining site using trains, five bucketwheel excavators and one stacker are supplied with power through a 3km overhead line. Excavators and stackers had to be converted from train to conveyor systems without major hold-ups. The equipment had to be interlocked with the belt conveyor system while follower control gear and safety devices were incorporated. Power supply to the drives was arranged through a central main switch station and kiosk type steel-clad stations.

entry.dc:title: GROUND PREPARATION BY RIPPING IN OPEN PIT MINING
entry.dc:creator: ATKINSON T
entry.dc:description: The advent of relatively inexpensive explosives such as ANFO and metallized slurries have resulted in considerable reductions in blasting costs so that some of the traditional roles of ripping are being challenged. S%At the same time more powerful and efficient machines are being developed and experience gained in ripping techniques so that continuous appraisal of ripping is appropriate. Ripper types and selection are analyzed. Rock qualification from the viewpoint of rippability and fracture index is discussed. Comparison of costs between ripping and blasting is discussed.

entry.dc:title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF KATANGA COPPER. GECOMIN'S OPEN PIT MINES ACHIEVE RECORD PRODUCTION
entry.dc:creator: WYLLIE RJM
entry.dc:description: General Congolaise des Minerais (Gecomin), nationalized successor of the former Union Miniere du Haut Kagangta, is responsible for the entire output of copper that with the 1969 production of 400,000 plus reached an all-time record. The individual five mining properties, the open pit mining methods and heavy equipment used are described. Trends of further development of production are discussed.

entry.dc:title: The pine point lead-zinc deposits, N.W.T., Canada introduction and paleocology of the presqu'ile reef
entry.dc:creator: Jackson S.
entry.dc:description: The zinc-lead deposits at Pine Point, N.W.T., comprise known ore reserves of 42.5 million tons averaging 7% Zn and 2.6% Pb in a 20 by 4 mile belt of barrier carbonate of Middle Devonian age, now exposed or at shallow depths amenable to open pit mining. Fore reef, reef and back reef facies in the Middle Devonian Pine Point, Presqu'ile and Sulphur Point Formations are recognizable in an elongate platform bounded on the north by the Mackenzie Shale basin and on the south by the Elk Point evaporites. During the development of this carbonate buildup the barrier platform was subject to periodic exposure, followed by renewed reef growth; ultimately late Middle Devonian and Upper Devonian transgressions of the sea caused the barrier buildup to be succeeded by carbonates of a more open marine character. The ore bodies that form an integral part of the upper Pine Point and the Presqu'ile formations are elongate lens shaped bodies ranging from a few hundred thousand to 10 million tons in size. Margins are sharp, most of the ore was deposited in open cavities and vugs. Colloform and crystalline sphalerite and galena are the only ore minerals; abundant marcasite, pyrite, calcite and dolomite comprise the gangue. Evaporites, deposited in a supratidal (Sabkha) environment, appear to have played a major role in the development of porosity that governed later dolomitization and ore emplacement. © 1969 Society of Economic Geologists, Inc.

entry.dc:title: TURKISH IRON ORE
entry.dc:creator: GUNEY M
entry.dc:description: S urvey of geographical location of known iron ore deposits in Turkey includes characteristic data about analysis of ore and reserves; most important deposit is that of Divrigi, located in NE province of Anatolia and containing magnetite and hematite ores of contactmetamorphic origin in mezozoic limestones, reserves of 40 to 45% Fe ore are estimated at 45 million tons; open pit mining produces about 900,000 tons/yr used by state owned Karabuk Iron and Steel Plant, located in vicinity of coal mines; trends of further expansion are indicated.

entry.dc:title: SOME DEVELOPMENTS IN POLISH OPEN PIT MINING
entry.dc:creator: ANON
entry.dc:description: In parallel with underground mining, during past ten yrs rapid development of opencast mining has taken place in Poland; at present nearly 200 million tons of ore and minerals are mined by opencast methods and approximately 150 million tons by underground mining; steadily increasing depth of mined mineral deposits, increasing productive capacity of single mine up to 50 million t/yr and introduction of large capacity belt conveying are main developments illustrated in case of sulfur open pit mine near Tarnobrzeg in Central Poland, producing presently 400,000 t/yr of pure S and Turow mine, near Czechoslovakia and East German borders, producing 15 million t/yr of lignite, with installed total length of belt conveyors amounting to 100 km.

entry.dc:title: CLAY MINERALOGY, FABRIC, AND INDUSTRIAL USES OF SHALE OF DECORAH FORMATION, SOUTHEASTERN MINNESOTA
entry.dc:creator: PARHAM WE
entry.dc:description: The Decorah shale varies both vertically and laterally in its clay mineral assemblages. It is principally an illitic shale in Minnesota, but kaolinite is approximately of equal abundance in the basal part to the southwest, reflecting nearness to the source area. Clay mineral data suggest that the Decorah shale may be satisfactory for use in ceramic products such as face brick, sewer pipe, light weight aggregate, structural tile, and drain tile. Numerous areas along the shale's outcrop belt in southeastern Minnesota would be satisfactory for open pit mining .

entry.dc:title: SULFUR MINING IN POLAND
entry.dc:creator: SINGHAL RK
entry.dc:description: Deposit, discovered in mid 1950's in Central Poland, on left bank of Vistula River extends over area of 11 sq mi and contains pure S reserves exceeding 100 million tons; S occurs in miocene limestone layer 5 to 10 m thick, covered by overburden 14 to 100 m thick; main problem facing open pit mining was purification of 2300 cu m/hr of contaminated with hydrogen sulfide, drainage water which could badly affect Vistula River vegetation; problem has been solved by aeration and recovery of elemental S from contaminated air; present production of ore, containing 21 to 24% S amount to 3 million tons per year, scheduled to reach in a few years 15 million tons per year; flowsheet of S production is included; excess of S over local consumption is exported in form of 99. 98% pure S.

entry.dc:title: BOUGAINVILLE COPPER WILL BE GIANT PIT IN HIGH MOUNTAIN RAIN FOREST
entry.dc:creator: ANON
entry.dc:description: Low grade Panguna porphyric orebody known to contain over 550x10**6 tons of ore assaying 0. 51% Cu and 0. 2 oz Au/ton is being developed by Australian mining interest for open pit mining designed to produce, beginning in 1972, 80,000 to 100,00 tpd of ore; about 13,100 ft long, 3900 ft wide and 1000 ft plus deep orebody is covered by up to 50 ft thick clayey type volcanic ash; access, heavy rainfall (up to 200 in. /yr), adequate tailing storage areas present some of many problems.

entry.dc:title: HOW ENGINEERING, EXPERIENCE, HIGH CAPACITY EQUIPMENT COMBINE TO MAKE ORE AT SIERRITA
entry.dc:creator: JANCIC T
entry.dc:description: Duval Sierrita Corp, subsidiary of Duval Corp is developing about 35 mi southwest of Tucson, Ariz, copper molybdenum ore body to be mined in open pit operation; deposit containing over 414x10//6 tons averaging 0. 35% Cu and 0. 036% Mo is covered by 634x10//6 tons of rocky overburden being removed from open pit designed with 45//0 final slopes; initial stage of development for production of 72,000 tpd requires removal of 105x10//6 tons of overburden; thereafter waste to ore ratio will gradually decline during first 10 yr of operation from 2. 25 to 0. 59; equipment required for open pit mining of 200,000 tpd ore and waste combined is listed; on straight copper basis, calculating Mo as Cu equipvalent, Cu grade of ore will average 0. 54%.

entry.dc:title: TRENDS IN TECHNICAL AND TECHNOLOGICAL DEVELOPMENT OF SURFACE COAL MINING IN USSR,
entry.dc:creator: KUSNEZOV KK
entry.dc:description: In 1966 141x10**6 tons of coal, or about 25% of total coal production, has been produced in open pit mines; total proven reserves of strippable coal in Soviet Union are estimated to amount to 140x10**9 tons; ratio of overburden in cu m to coal in tons rose from 3. 0 (1950) to 3. 75 (1965); mean production of 62 surface mines amounted in 1966 to 2. 4x10**6 tons/yr; output per man and month is given as 275. 2 tons against 40. 2 tons in underground mines; excavating equipment used in open pit mining is described.

entry.dc:title: MOROCCAN PHOSPHATE. UNDERGROUND AND OPEN PIT MINING, SOME ORE IS BENEFICIATED BY WASHING, DRY BEFORE SHIPPING
entry.dc:creator: ARGALL GO
entry.dc:description: Description of Khouribga Mining Complex operated by Morocco's Office Cheriffien des Phosphates (OCP); reserves of phosphates calculated at 40x10//9 tonnes mined by mechanized open pit and underground methods of permitted OCP to become in 1967 largest exporter of phosphates in world with 9. 8-million tonnes exported; presently top bed 1. 2 to 2. 5 m thick, laying at depth of 120 ft is mined underground by continuous retreat room and apillar stoping, recovering about 80% of ore, containing about 34% P//2O//5; open pit ore is washed, all ore is dried down to about 15% of moisture; ore treatment plants are described.

entry.dc:title: SURFACE SUBSIDENCE WITHIN RANGE OF LIGNITE OPEN PIT MINING AS EFFECT OF WATER TABLE LOWERING,
entry.dc:creator: RUDOLF H
entry.dc:description: Effect has been investigated in two lignite open pits in East Germany; equations have been developed to anticipate magnitude of subsidence and actual measurements have been found to vary about 33%; it has been ascertained by regression method that proposed method to figure out in advance amount of subsidence is sufficiently accurate if geological structural data, probable drawdown of water table and soil mechanical characteristics, are available.

entry.dc:title: STRUCTURAL GEOLOGY AS BASIS FOR PLANNING OF OPEN PIT MINING OPERATIONS,
entry.dc:creator: WEBER H
entry.dc:description: Exploitation of knowledge of structural characteristics of rock masses can be used as potential contribution to decreasing cost of mining; to accomplish that purpose it appears to be necessary to- collect structural measuring data prior to beginning of mining, measuring behavior of rock masses during maining and, experimenting in situ and with models; measuring instruments are described.
